observations: Photo 0 and 1 show a dismantled automotive manual transmission/gearbox assembly, cast metal casing, dirty with grease and dust, laid directly on concrete pavement.
A barcode and a printed label are visible on the casing in both photos, but the text is too small/blurred to read any part number, VIN, or manufacturer code.
A watermark 'KENELIX AUTOTECH LIMITED' appears across both images - this is the seller's business branding, not a manufacturer mark on the item.
Output/input shaft splines are visible at one end (photo 0), appearing intact but corroded with surface rust/grime.
A loose cable or sensor wire dangles from the top of the casing in both photos, connector end not clearly shown.
No vehicle, engine bay, or chassis context is shown - only the standalone unit on pavement next to a person's sandaled foot.
No fluid, no stamped logo (e.g. Toyota, Nissan, Mercedes) legible in either photo.

claims.claim: "This gear box is like no other"
claims.evidence: Vague marketing language, no measurable or checkable attribute shown in either photo.

risks.risk: Vehicle make/model/engine fitment unknown, which drives most of the value for a used gearbox.
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the stamped part number/label or a photo of the gearbox mounted in/matched to the donor vehicle.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unidentified generic used gearbox, lowest tier of comparable fitment value

risks.risk: Internal condition (gear wear, synchro wear, bearing noise) cannot be seen from exterior photos.
risks.proof: Video of the input/output shaft being turned by hand showing smooth gear engagement, or a bench/spin test clip.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / condition unknown

risks.risk: Casing shows corrosion and grime; possible water or long outdoor exposure damage to seals/bearings.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of seals, bell housing interior, and any rust pitting on shaft.

risks.risk: Dangling sensor/cable of unknown function - could indicate a missing connector or damaged wiring harness stub.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the connector end and confirmation it is a factory sensor (e.g., speed/reverse switch) still functional.

risks.risk: No proof gearbox turns freely or is not seized/locked.
risks.proof: Video showing shaft rotation and gear shifting by hand.

proof_requests: Clear, well-lit close-up photo of the part number/label and barcode sticker.
Photo or video showing the gearbox's donor vehicle (make, model, or chassis plate) for fitment confirmation.
Video of input/output shaft rotation and gear shifting by hand.
Close-up of seals and bell housing interior for wear/damage assessment.
Clear photo of the dangling connector/sensor to identify its function and condition.
response.reason: The item type is clear (a used manual gearbox) but its value is overwhelmingly determined by vehicle fitment and part number, both of which are present on the casing labels but unreadable in the photos; without that, even a worst-case price cannot be meaningfully set.
